redactions.original: Held: Since P did not attach to her return any Form 8332 or equivalent release, P is not entitled under I.R.C. sec. 152(e)(2)(A) to claim the dependency exemption
Held, further: P is not entitled to the HOH filing status under I.R.C. sec. 2(b)(1).
The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) determined a deficiency of $4,377 in the 2014 Federal income tax
On these issues we hold for the IRS.
Opinion parts I-IV (pages 8-18): ... she is not entitled to the dependency exemption deductions ... not entitled to a child tax credit ... not entitled to HOH filing status.
Decision will be entered for respondent.

facts_from_discussion: Ms. Bethune admits that N.K. and C.K. did not share the same place of abode with her for more than one-half of 2014; both resided with their father, Mr. Kirby, for more than one-half of 2014.
Mr. Kirby was the custodial parent and Ms. Bethune was the noncustodial parent of N.K. and C.K. for 2014.
In his July 2015 statement Mr. Kirby did not state that he would not claim N.K. and C.K. as dependents; the statement said only that Ms. Bethune "will" claim them.

Mr. Kirby's July 2015 statement made forward-looking assertions about what "will continue to be claimed" and what "will be claimed", and assertions about years "prior to 2014 tax year", but did not address the 2014 year.
Mr. Kirby did claim N.K. and C.K. on his 2014 return, and he did not undertake in the July 2015 statement to do otherwise or to undo that claim.
The court found that Mr. Kirby did sign the Form 8332 dated April 12, 2017, as Ms. Bethune alleged.

Ms. Bethune filed a paper (not electronic) 2014 return and did not attach the Form 8332 (or any other declaration) to that return; she first provided the Form 8332 to the IRS on May 1, 2017, shortly after the SNOD was issued.
The custodial parent (Mr. Kirby) never relinquished his own 2014 claim to the dependency exemptions and never filed an amended return removing that claim.
